shared_elements: concentric ring / circle motif carved in relief-outline
large ringed eye-like discs in a pair
curved grooved arcs framing a face or body
broad curved band of parallel incised lines
justification: Both surfaces carry the same distinctive vocabulary of deeply grooved concentric ring discs set in pairs beneath sweeping curved arcs, attached to a schematic anthropomorphic face/body with no interior infill, which is a more specific correspondence than a generic circle. The biggest difference is the compositional scope: A is a single frontal mask-like face filling the field with the rings functioning as eyes, whereas B is a whole standing figure whose ring motifs sit on the torso above a banded belt-like girdle, with the actual face rendered separately as a three-dimensional head.
